memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, a smoking firepot with a blazing torch appeared and passed between the pieces. On that day the Lord made a covenant with Abram... - Gen 15:17-18a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the most astonishing moment in the chapter. In an ancient covenant, both parties walked between the pieces, pledging their lives to keep their word. But look at what happens here. Abram is asleep. Only God passes through - a smoking firepot and blazing torch, symbols of His presence, moving alone between the severed animals.

God walks the covenant path by Himself. He takes the entire obligation on His own shoulders. He is saying, in the starkest terms available: If this covenant is broken, let it fall on Me.

Sit with the weight of that. God pledged Himself to keep a promise that fallen human beings would inevitably break - and He accepted the consequences in advance. He signed a contract knowing the other party would default, and agreed to pay for it.

And that is precisely what happened at Calvary. When the covenant was broken by us, the curse fell on Him. "Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us" (Gal 3:13). The blazing torch that walked alone through the darkness for Abram was pointing to a cross where God Himself bore what we deserved. Your salvation rests on a covenant God made - and kept - alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you grasp that God took your covenant obligations onto Himself?
- How does it change things to know your salvation rests on God's promise, not your performance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You walked the covenant path alone and took my obligations on Yourself. Thank You that at the cross Jesus bore what I deserved. My salvation rests on Your promise, not my performance.
Amen.
